opportunities.name: Mana-surge stun attack
opportunities.objective: Test a deliberate energized attack after E stun as a resource-positive trade.
opportunities.mechanic: Mana Surge restores twice the non-champion amount on a champion attack, on a sixteen-second clock reduced by kills. E stuns up to 2.25 seconds depending on flight distance; RFC extends one attack and Lich Bane adds a separate magic packet after a cast. AP still strengthens Q/W, while Cosmic can support retreat after the hit.
opportunities.requiredState: Passive and energized attack ready; E connects and attacker can reach within the stun.
opportunities.failure: Approaching to attack forfeits artillery safety and wastes the low-AD crit slot.
opportunities.test: Compare E-one-attack-Q with spell-only poke, logging mana restored, attack range and damage taken.
opportunities.rejectedAssumption: RFC extends the charged attack, not Xerath Q/E cast range.

opportunities.name: Artillery hit ladder
opportunities.objective: Preserve R hit accuracy while testing debuffs around its per-hit damage growth.
opportunities.mechanic: R fires four to six times and adds AP-scaled damage per champion hit, so later shots depend on actual earlier connections. Horizon reveals targets struck from at least 600 range; Malignance can test Hatefog/MR reduction for R damage and Bloodletter tests debuff ramp. W center slow and E stun help prepare the channel rather than assuming every shot lands.
opportunities.requiredState: Record R rank, shot count, hits and distance; a safe ten-second channel is possible.
opportunities.failure: An interrupted channel or moving target causes misses and removes the claimed shot ladder.
opportunities.test: Measure shot-by-shot damage and MR debuff after a miss versus a connected opening hit.
opportunities.rejectedAssumption: Horizon current catalog is a reveal effect, not an assumed generic damage amplification.

ruledOut.idea: Passive restores mana on every attack
ruledOut.reason: Mana Surge has a sixteen-second cooldown with kill reductions; repeated attacks alone do not reset it.

unknowns: R hit-ladder scope across different victims and Hatefog refresh need live validation; charged-attack item set is a narrow experiment.

AP still strengthens Q/W, while Cosmic can support retreat after the hit.
testPlan: Required state: Passive and energized attack ready; E connects and attacker can reach within the stun.
Compare E-one-attack-Q with spell-only poke, logging mana restored, attack range and damage taken.

Run three trials at matched level, ranks, gold and target defenses. Repeat against a moving opponent with a fixed incoming damage pattern. Record damage packets, missed actions, resource cost and survival separately.
Keep souls, health/mana, form, item/rune stacks, transformations and game time finite and explicitly recorded. No free full ramp or infinite scaling.
failureConditions: Approaching to attack forfeits artillery safety and wastes the low-AD crit slot.
The narrow damage gain does not repay lost access, survival, wave control or allied utility.
tradeoffs: Rejected assumption: RFC extends the charged attack, not Xerath Q/E cast range.
Confidence: speculative. Source-compatible reasoning is not in-game validation or proof of novelty/optimality.
buyOrder: Candidate six slots: Rapid Firecannon, Lich Bane, Luden's Echo, Cosmic Drive, Void Staff, Sorcerer's Shoes. Compare two-item checkpoints before the final six-slot test; this list is not a lane shopping order.
Keep role-appropriate starters, boots and support quest/vision obligations. If the full candidate assumes farmed income, compare it separately from support income.
coverageNotes: Only Cassiopeia Q/E and Sett W have numerical adapters. Even there, these other objectives and item/rune interactions may fall outside the model.
Proc inheritance, crit, pet hits and conditional helpers remain uncertain until observed. No completed mathematical maximum is claimed.

kitEvidence.formula:
Begin Charging: Xerath begins charging an arcane beam, Slowing himself gradually up to 50%. 

Release: Xerath fires the beam, dealing [70 / 110 / 150 / 190 / 230 + (0.9) × AP] magic damage. The range increases with time charged.
Xerath fires an orb of raw magic, Stunning the first enemy hit for up to [2.25] seconds based on distance travelled, and dealing [70 / 100 / 130 / 160 / 190 + (0.45) × AP] magic damage.

Every 16 seconds Xerath's next Attack against a champion restores [(characterLevelBreakpoints(start=30, perLevel=3, changes=[{"mLevel": 4, "mBonusPerLevelAtAndAfter": 6.0, "__type": "Breakpoint"}, {"mLevel": 7, "mBonusPerLevelAtAndAfter": 9.0, "__type": "Breakpoint"}, {"mLevel": 11, "mBonusPerLevelAtAndAfter": 12.0, "__type": "Breakpoint"}, {"mLevel": 16, "mBonusPerLevelAtAndAfter": 15.0, "__type": "Breakpoint"}])) × (2)] Mana. It restores [characterLevelBreakpoints(start=30, perLevel=3, changes=[{"mLevel": 4, "mBonusPerLevelAtAndAfter": 6.0, "__type": "Breakpoint"}, {"mLevel": 7, "mBonusPerLevelAtAndAfter": 9.0, "__type": "Breakpoint"}, {"mLevel": 11, "mBonusPerLevelAtAndAfter": 12.0, "__type": "Breakpoint"}, {"mLevel": 16, "mBonusPerLevelAtAndAfter": 15.0, "__type": "Breakpoint"}])] Mana if attacking minions, jungle monsters or structures.

Whenever Xerath kills a unit, this cooldown is reduced by [3.5] seconds.

Xerath calls down a blast of arcane energy, dealing [50 / 85 / 120 / 155 / 190 + (0.65) × AP] magic damage and Slowing them by [25]% for [2.5] seconds. Enemies in the center take [(50 / 85 / 120 / 155 / 190 + (0.65) × AP) × (1.667)] magic damage instead and are Slowed by [(0.6 / 0.65 / 0.7 / 0.75 / 0.8) × 100]%, decaying over [2.5] seconds.
